Durable interruption recovery: precise product behavior

The obligation being recovered

The first registered kind is terminal-harvest. A workflow discovers a bounded, eligible follow-up and records the obligation before depending on conversation retention. The record contains enough sanitized information to re-present or reconcile that exact candidate. Registration is ordinary local bookkeeping for already authorized work. It is not a decision to create a task, change an open question, publish an issue, accept an ADR, finish work, approve review, or delete anything.

The existing terminal step remains where the workflow applies its harvest policy. The change is that an interrupted workflow has a durable local continuation. Registration at terminal time alone would reproduce the defect. Conversely, the implementation must not claim to recover a finding that was never successfully registered. A failed registration reports durable: false with a bounded reason and allows independent work to continue.

Known producer sites are the TDD Phase 6 findings, brainstorming and planning triage findings, commit-gate set-asides, checkpoint DEFERRABLE findings, and low-confidence sprint decisions identified in core/surface/includes/harvest.md. The same registered-kind architecture can later support a specific ordinary continuation, but this release does not grant a generic instruction-replay facility. An unregistered kind is unavailable and cannot supply executable code, arbitrary target paths, or shell text to the runner.

Storage and ownership

Add a shared Python owner, proposed as core/pysrc/_workflowrecoverylib.py, and a bounded CLI, proposed as core/pysrc/workflow-recovery.py. Put the closed schema and kind declarations in proposed core/workflow-recovery-contract.json, following the repository's existing root core/*-contract.json pattern. These are proposed new paths, not claims about existing files.

Store records under the repository's resolved Git-common directory in an owned codearbiter/workflow-recovery/v1/ subtree. Use the existing safe Git-common/worktree resolution patterns from _artifactauthoritylib.py and _reconciliationlib.py; do not accept a caller-provided arbitrary storage root in installed operation. Bind each record to the repository instance, its selected native project identity when present, the originating worktree, and an exact workflow run. A Git-common store survives interruption and branch switching locally. It is not portable work evidence, a cloud backup, or a claim of durability after deletion of that repository's Git directory.

Git-common placement avoids inventing a new .codearbiter document kind. Register the new runtime path and owner explicitly in the product's storage/inventory/cleanup/doctor documentation and relevant packaging checks. Native snapshot/evidence policies already exclude Git metadata (core/artifacts/internal/validate/input_policy.go); preserve that exclusion. No plan may cite recovery bookkeeping as reviewed input or completion evidence. If a later implementation adds a native consumer or a .codearbiter projection, that is an explicit additional registry/schema task and must be admitted by every relevant reader before it ships.

The local owner must validate exact path containment, directory/file type, and the same symlink/ownership requirements used by comparable protected spools. Reads must not follow a caller-supplied path out of the owned subtree. Registration and transition writes use an OS-held lock, revision compare-and-swap, atomic replace, and a durable commit result that distinguishes written, observed, and durability-uncertain outcomes. Do not claim no effect merely because an error occurred after the commit point; _planfilelib.py is an existing example of that distinction.

Use canonical records keyed by obligation ID with a bounded paged index. Index maintenance is part of a recoverable write transaction, not an independent best-effort write that can permanently hide an acknowledged record. A small durable write intent under the writer lock can recover the record/index pair; prove each interruption point. Automatic read-only scans inspect the bounded transaction header before an index page and report partial/unavailable when repair is needed; the explicit recovery/write path performs the repair under its lock. Readers never translate an unreadable or incomplete index into “nothing pending.” This is a file protocol, not a new database service.

Minimal closed record

Field group Required meaning
Version and kind Exact schema version and an installed registered kind, initially terminal-harvest. Unknown versions are preserved and reported unavailable.
Identity Repository-local ID; native project_id if already available; worktree identity; workflow_run_id; stable obligation_id; exact source origin including its item suffix.
Work binding Native work ID, exact legacy origin/row identity, or explicit none for authorized ordinary work without an enrolled task. Do not require task creation merely to register recovery.
Source binding Workflow/phase, source locator, source fingerprint, and source branch/base observations where relevant. Branch names are observations, not sufficient identity.
Candidate Bounded sanitized title/description, work/decision kind, blocking classification, and provenance. Store no full transcript, raw debug packet, secret, credential, raw rejected payload, or arbitrary command.
Lifecycle State, monotonically increasing record revision, created/updated timestamps, reason code, previous attempt linkage, and explicit last transition. Time is diagnostic, not permission.
Claim Attempt ID, host/session and process-instance identity, claim nonce, expected record revision, and intended effect operation ID. The claim is not an authorization grant.
Effect binding Selected owner, target kind, exact origin, immutable candidate revision, operation ID, and expected target revision/hash when the target supports them.
Outcome Observed target identity and receipt/digest; disposition such as promoted, reused, explicitly declined, superseded, or explicitly cancelled; evidence for that disposition.

Do not persist “authorized: true” as a reusable permission ticket. Record the relevant authority source or scoped parent delegation reference only as context and revalidate the actual current host/user boundary at effect time. Registering or reading a local obligation must not require a new user approval ceremony. Existing interactive harvest confirmation remains specific to promotion; an already authorized sprint may use its existing in-scope promotion authority. Revocation, actual denial, an explicit stop, or a changed scope continues to constrain the affected effect.

Three identities, with different jobs

  1. Obligation ID is stable across discovery replay, process restart, and session reentry. Derive it from canonical repository/workflow/kind/exact-origin identity, or persist an opaque ID with an exact unique origin index. Do not derive it from a timestamp or the current session alone.
  2. Candidate revision changes when an authorized correction changes the proposed content. Compare-and-swap protects a concurrent edit; the old candidate remains in transition history. A new revision does not overwrite an effect of unknown outcome.
  3. Effect operation ID binds obligation ID, candidate revision, target owner, and requested action. The exact retry uses the same ID and immutable payload. A corrected attempt gets a new linked identity only after the earlier effect is known absent or settled. Target origin deduplication remains a second defense across different workflow runs.

The target operation's real idempotency contract governs retries. Native work creation can use its stable operation identity and exact origin. Legacy work origin deduplication is also valuable, but _worklib.LegacyClient does not become a durable operation ledger just because a caller passes an operation ID. After an ambiguous result, look up the exact origin through the selected owner before retrying. Never select a same-title item or choose a different writer as fallback.

State × event × side effect contract

unavailable is a durable unresolved state, not a synonym for discarded or denied. Its reason distinguishes temporary I/O, unsupported version, changed binding, actual authorization denial, corrupt evidence, and an uncertain previous effect. The diagnostic must give the next legitimate action without implying that every reason can be solved by resubmission.

State Event and guard Next state Required side effects and failure behavior
Absent Eligible candidate discovered; closed kind/schema and bounded bindings valid pending Durably register before claiming success. Same identity and same candidate return existing state. No task/issue/decision write.
Absent Invalid, oversize, unknown-kind input or storage unavailable Absent; unavailable result Return bounded sanitized diagnostics and durable: false. Ordinary unrelated work continues. Do not invent a persisted record.
pending Same registration arrives again pending Return existing ID/revision; no duplicate or rewritten candidate. Different payload is a conflict/correction request, not idempotent success.
pending Authorized correction, expected revision matches, no unknown effect pending at new revision Record corrected candidate and prior linkage. No authority or source truth is invented to make validation pass.
pending Startup, prompt reentry, status, or standup scan pending Read a bounded summary; expose pending count/partial scan and a resume route. Never execute promotion, cleanup, publication, or review automatically.
pending Workflow terminal step or explicit resume; current binding and actual effect authority hold; per-obligation lock acquired claimed Persist claim and immutable effect intent before calling the target adapter. A duplicate claimant returns busy/current state.
pending Target ownership ambiguous, source stale, unsupported kind/version, actual scope denied, or required material unavailable unavailable Retain candidate and precise reason. Pause only this dependent effect. Do not fall back to a second owner or request universal approval.
pending Interactive preview declined settled: declined only after its local audit event is durable Write one idempotent decline event and terminal receipt; no board/question write. If audit commit is uncertain, retain a recoverable attempt.
claimed Effect not yet attempted; process remains live claimed The OS-held per-obligation lock prevents another executor. A timestamp is not proof the owner died.
claimed Target reports success and exact target readback proves effect or exact-origin reuse settled: promoted/reused Persist target ID and outcome receipt. Do not infer parent work completion, review pass, merge, or cleanup.
claimed Target response lost or process dies after effect may have committed claimed, then reconciliation A later executor acquires the released OS lock and queries exact operation/origin. It never blindly replays an unknown effect.
claimed Reconciliation proves exact intended effect exists settled: promoted/reused Record recovered receipt; no duplicate write. Existing independently edited content is not overwritten.
claimed Reconciliation proves effect did not commit and current binding/authority still hold pending or a new claimed attempt Preserve the immutable effect identity for exact retry; record the failed attempt. No new permission is fabricated.
claimed Outcome cannot be determined, target unavailable, or source/authority changed unavailable Retain unresolved effect intent and reason. New revisions and effects wait for reconciliation of this obligation only.
claimed Another session presents a live/busy claim claimed Report busy with bounded metadata; no TTL-based theft or global session wait.
unavailable Read-only status/reentry unavailable Show reason and the legitimate recovery route. Suppress repeated identical notices within the session without discarding state.
unavailable Relevant condition changes; current bindings and real authority revalidated; previous effect reconciled pending Record reason-specific recovery. A formatting correction alone cannot clear an authorization denial or explicit stop.
unavailable Unknown schema or malformed on-disk record unavailable Preserve bytes under owned access; no automatic overwrite, deletion, downgrade, or empty-state interpretation. Report only bounded safe metadata.
pending / unavailable Explicit authorized cancellation or supersession, with no unreconciled effect settled: cancelled/superseded Retain disposition and link to replacement if any. An absent source or elapsed time alone is insufficient.
settled Exact registration, retry, or notification replay settled Return the terminal receipt/tombstone and target link; no repeated effect or prompt.
settled New authorized follow-up after changed facts New linked obligation/attempt Keep old history immutable. Do not reopen the old receipt or pretend the previous outcome never happened.
Any persisted state Record/index write fails after a possible commit point Observed state or explicit uncertain result Re-read/reconcile; report requested, observed, committed/durable facts separately. Never silently revert a later writer.

There is no age-triggered pending → settled transition, no error → complete transition, and no validation-pass → authorization-granted transition.

Claims and interruption recovery

Hold a per-obligation OS lock for the entire local adapter execution and reconciliation window. Keep the global index/writer lock short. An adapter cannot release the only liveness lock and continue mutating while another process is allowed to recover it. If cross-process execution requires a different lock protocol, its owner-instance binding and cancellation semantics must be proved in the same change; a stale timestamp alone is insufficient.

On restart, a persisted claim plus an available OS lock means the previous critical section is no longer held. It does not prove that the target effect failed. The handler first reads the exact selected target and operation/origin identity. Only observed target state decides whether to settle, retry, or report unavailable. An unavailable target never permits a speculative second write.

For a batch, each candidate has its own obligation and outcome. One failed candidate does not erase successfully settled candidates or hold unrelated work hostage. The batch summary names completed, retained, and unavailable IDs. It must not say the entire harvest succeeded merely because one helper returned zero.

Target adapters and original workflow rules

Target Allowed effect Idempotency and authorization
Native work Create/reuse the exact origin using work.py, or report a current refusal. Preserve the native operation ID, current owner/project identity, and exact-origin lookup across active/archive. Never downgrade to a legacy writer.
Legacy work Use the sanctioned taskwrite.py/work owner route and existing exact-origin behavior. Re-read origin across open/archive after uncertainty; keep locking and archive-first semantics. An operation ID echo is not proof of durable execution.
Nonblocking decision Append a deferred decision through a narrowly scoped, idempotent writer. If no existing writer can supply a stable origin/event ID and CAS/readback, implement that adapter before enabling automatic retry. Do not append duplicate prose on every resume.
Blocking decision Present the existing escalation/resolution route. Registration is allowed; automatic confirmation and automatic promotion are not. Pause only work actually depending on that unresolved decision.
Declined promotion Append one bounded local decline event with stable identity. An explicit decline settles this candidate only after its audit outcome is durable; it is not a broad refusal of independent work.
GitHub issue or any external publication No recovery-time automatic effect. Existing explicit publication authority and workflow apply. Pending local recovery does not authorize sending information or creating remote records.

Preserve the current harvest rule that candidates are contingent on the work unless the workflow explicitly establishes otherwise. A pending record may survive an interrupted or abandoned branch locally, but that survival does not make a follow-up authoritative on another branch. Reentry must revalidate the source/work binding. A candidate that should survive abandonment can be routed to the existing issue workflow under its actual publication authority; the scanner must not create the issue itself.

Commit-gate's harvest still occurs before explicit staging so promoted work can travel with its originating work commit, as ADR0008 requires. Startup does not stage any path. Nothing in the recovery ledger marks a work item done or changes the commit candidate. Ordinary discovery bookkeeping can be durable locally without becoming a committed project artifact.

Startup, reentry, and user experience

Use one shared summary projection across session-start.py, relevant prompt/reentry paths, the status/standup flows, and the host adapters. Read an existing ledger only for an already active project. A dormant project must not be activated and must not gain a new recovery directory just because a hook ran. Explicit status/recovery can show missing/legacy state honestly.

Proposed hard data bounds are 32 record summaries and 256 KiB per automatic scan, with at most 64 KiB per candidate registration and 32 candidates in one producer batch. These are implementation acceptance limits, not claims about current performance. Payloads that exceed them require explicit bounded batching or a visible unavailable outcome; never silently truncate a candidate into a different obligation. The scan returns complete, partial, or unavailable plus an opaque continuation cursor and observed counts. An unknown total is reported as unknown. A count from a partial scan is a lower bound, not a complete backlog count.

Use a versioned paged index so scanning one page does not enumerate and sort the entire history. A cursor binds index generation and page identity; stale cursors restart a bounded read or report a changed inventory. Before shipping, measure the scan within the actual host startup budget and add timeout handling at existing host boundaries. Do not promise a hard wall-clock limit for arbitrary filesystem I/O merely because the loop checks a deadline.

Display a concise actionable notice, for example: “2 follow-ups from the interrupted fix await harvest; 1 is unavailable because its source changed. Resume these items or keep working.” The recovery status is a projection of the durable ledger, not the truth owner. Suppress the same notice after delivery for the same session/ledger revision, but a mode switch, compaction, or dedup bug must never delete the underlying record. A failed notification does not mean the obligation was settled.

New-session recovery is supported without pretending that a new session owns the old session's grants. The new session can inspect the local pending record and reconcile already attempted effects. It can apply a new effect only within its current real authority. Pi child registration must be bounded to the parent delegation's work/run/origin scope through PI-D01–PI-D05; its durable observation can feed the shared notice, but recovery never restores a revoked grant. Claude/Codex/Pi should present the same semantic result through their own supported event seams.

Retention, upgrades, and rollback

Unresolved obligations never disappear because they are old, a budget was exceeded, a branch was deleted, or an agent said “done.” Retain pending/claimed/unavailable state until an observed target effect or an explicit authorized terminal disposition settles it. At capacity, registration reports that it was not durable; it does not evict an older unresolved item. This design bounds individual records and work per read; it does not falsely promise a fixed lifetime disk footprint for an indefinitely retained history.

Settled records may be compacted to small immutable tombstones containing operation/origin identity, terminal disposition, target reference, and receipt digest. Preserve exact ID lookup and deduplication after compaction. Compaction writes and verifies the replacement/index before removing redundant owned bytes. Do not delete a live target, worktree, branch, unrelated transcript, or pending record as part of ledger maintenance. Retention/archival is local runtime housekeeping, not an exception to destructive cleanup authorization. If an implementation wants to relax ADR0036's cleanup confirmation clause, that belongs to the separate independently reviewed cleanup backend and a successor ADR; this design supplies no such relaxation.

Absence of a ledger means “no registered obligations,” not “all historical workflows completed.” Do not bulk-mine old conversations, full logs, or arbitrary plans at startup. Any optional legacy residue import must be an explicit bounded operation using source checksums and exact origins, with current owner deduplication and visible uncertainty. Old versions must ignore the new owned runtime directory without deleting it. Unknown schema versions remain readable only as bounded unavailable metadata; do not overwrite them with a lower version. Rollback disables new writers/notifications while preserving the ledger and target records. Retain an explicit version-compatible export/recovery path; reverting source is not a transaction rollback of effects already observed.

Failure-injection acceptance matrix

Interruption or conflict Required observation after restart
Before any durable registration No claimed recovery guarantee; the producer reports durable: false when it observed failure.
Record written, index transaction incomplete The bounded recovery header repairs or reports unavailable; an acknowledged registration is never silently absent.
Registration response lost Exact ID/origin replay returns the existing record, with no duplicate.
Claim written, target not called Reconciliation proves absence, then permits the exact authorized retry.
Target committed, response lost Exact-origin/operation readback settles once; no duplicate task or question.
Target committed, settlement write fails The record remains recoverable and the next read records the existing target.
Two sessions race to claim/correct/settle One expected revision wins; the loser observes conflict/busy and preserves the winner.
Source changed while pending Only this candidate becomes unavailable until current context resolves it.
Active target owner changes or dual ownership appears No fallback writer; affected promotion is unavailable.
Claiming process dies / live process is slow Dead critical section can reconcile; live lock cannot be stolen based on time.
Explicit denial or revoked Pi parent delegation The pending record persists; no new effect; unrelated authorized work continues.
Malformed/unknown-version record or stale cursor Bounded diagnostic and partial/unavailable inventory; no “clean” summary and no destructive repair.
Partial batch and full scan budget Exact completed/remaining IDs and continuation; no global completion or inferred empty queue.
Compaction/rollback/host reinstall Tombstone deduplication and unresolved records survive; no replay of external effects.

Corrected debug and reviewer submissions

Debug

The current _debughandofflib.py is a stateless validator. debug-handoff.py accepts bounded input and reports exit 2 for input/shape/reference/internal-semantic failures, exit 3 for operational failures, and exit 0 for a valid packet. None of these facts independently proves a causal claim, the current runtime, or permission to repair. Keep the bounded schema, field paths, sanitized diagnostics, and full causal/regression obligations.

Replace the blanket no-resubmission sentences in core/surface/skills/debug/SKILL.md and references/preparation.md. A correction may address a reported input defect, stale binding after new observation, or operational recovery. It must name what changed, preserve the known case history, and distinguish observed facts from proposed repairs. Do not treat every exit 2 as “format only”; semantic failures may require new evidence or a different disposition. An unchanged retry without a changed condition is not progress. Do not switch interpreters or alternate validators to bypass the installed owner.

The normal successful debug handoff remains a bounded packet and summary. Do not introduce a persistent debug packet store merely to implement resubmission. The terminal-harvest ledger may retain a sanitized follow-up obligation, not the complete diagnosis or rejected payload. If the validator is unavailable, the transfer remains unvalidated; correcting presentation does not authorize a code fix or manufacture a failing regression.

Reviewer

core/surface/agents/authority-reviewer.md prohibits retry under the same request. It does not prove that all future review requests are prohibited. Preserve immutable request finality. A corrected submission uses a new linked request/attempt where the current adapter consumes or rejects the old one; it captures the current frozen target, contract, context, host child launch, coverage, and actual first terminal event. An exact transport replay of an unchanged immutable successful operation uses its original operation ID.

Native task NT-11 verifies compatibility. The native authority-bearing review schema admits a valid observed pass; changes_requested is not a success receipt. The existing native validator binds host profile, captured launch, target/context, contract, coverage, and assessment. Prefer the existing observation formats with a fresh truthful launch when sufficient; do not add ad hoc retry fields to closed old schemas. A later stop from the same child cannot be relabeled first_stop. Keep rejected, denied, failed, and changes-requested history; never mutate an old refusal into approval.

A correction can repair the report or respond to actual findings. It cannot remove an actual user denial, relax tool scope, claim independence after steering, pass missing evidence, or convert a HIGH finding into a nonblocking result without the separately selected policy. Apply the distinction to common review output and diagnostics, not only to the debug route.

ADR and policy changes

Accepted ADR bodies are part of the repository's append-only decision history. Do not silently rewrite an accepted body to make history agree with the new implementation. Use the installed ADR workflow and current acceptance/implementation ledger: allocate successor numbers at implementation time, record exact scoped supersession, attribute the user-selected decisions, and attach implementation and verification evidence only after it exists.

Current owner Required decision update Explicit boundary
ADR0030, orchestration mode plane Scoped successor clarifies selected/raw/backed effective mode, transition identity, persona delivery, compaction generation, and truthful partial audit outcome. Correct the contradictory gates-on/off language. Deterministic guards remain mode-independent. Delivery does not prove the model consumed or forgot earlier persona text.
ADR0043, assistive state engine Add a scoped implementation clarification/successor for dependent-only conflict pauses and durable nonblocking bookkeeping/reentry. Do not decide the separate progress/evidence SMARTS question here; no new universal approval gate or database.
ADR0008, board-sync chokepoint Clarify that local pending capture can precede terminal harvest and survive interruption while promotion/staging still respects branch contingency and the work commit. No automatic cross-branch promotion, issue publication, board completion, or staging.
ADR0036, cleanup direction Record that recovery-ledger retention does not supersede per-item/group cleanup authority. Link the host cleanup successor only if that workstream actually implements and independently reviews its backend. The user-approved recovery feature is not permission to delete worktrees/branches or weaken deletion proof.
Debug/review policy owners Record corrected-submission permission, error categories, and immutable attempt linkage in a focused decision if required by current accepted policy. Actual denial, evidence freshness, reviewer independence, and scope controls remain separate.
Common reviewer/dependency policy (W-F03) B and receiving agent choose maintenance-only HIGH disposition; then update both owners and generated summaries in one change. Not settled by corrected resubmission. Until chosen, preserve/reveal the conflict for the affected review.
Compatibility policy (W-F09) Make the existing major/1.0 floor plus separately approved named removal and fresh release evidence the one machine-readable rule. No alias removal is included in this plan. If B chooses a different rule, make that explicit before implementation.

The operating corpus should record these as accepted user directions, proposed implementation choices, or unresolved choices accurately. Do not label a drafted ADR accepted, an implemented reducer verified, or a tested source release-qualified before the respective evidence exists.

Mode and installer corrections

For persona delivery, model a transition epoch or equivalent current delivered-state identity, not the historical set of every mode ever delivered during a session. The epoch must advance only for a real selected/effective transition, remain stable for duplicate host events, and cooperate with the compaction generation. Include arbiter → dangerous → arbiter, ops → arbiter → ops, repeated same-mode tokens, duplicate prompts, new sessions, and compaction during transitions. Retain exact whole-prompt token recognition and owed audit behavior.

For mode outcomes, keep requested, raw persisted, ledger-backed effective, and delivered state distinct. An audit append failure after a raw marker commit must report that partial result and its recovery, not “session remains unchanged.” The existing owed-audit mechanism must converge on replay without duplicate rows or bypassing backing checks. Status text must never claim that dangerous/ops mode disabled deterministic gates.

For spinner uninstall, store the exact installed owned value separately from the prior backup. Restore the backup only if the current setting equals that owned value; otherwise preserve the user's later value and report that ownership ended. Handle missing settings, partial backups, repeated uninstall, upgrade from older backup shapes, and unchanged statusLine ownership independently. Never replace a whole settings object to fix one key.

The Pi doctor correction must use the real scoped package identity and host/package source while retaining all independent checks for version, extension, skills, and package discovery. Do not change the package's public name to fit a broken diagnostic. The launch binding correction must land with NT-04: the actual POSIX probe produced 32/33/34 launch files for 30/31/32 workspaces; the source-supported Windows maximum is 37. Preserve the 32 workspace-manifest role bound and real launch fingerprints; do not make all collections unbounded to admit a legitimate producer result.

Generated surfaces and compatibility

Correct factual descriptions at their source and generate derivatives. GEN-F01 changes the nudge explanation to the runtime's freed-context predicate. It does not change when the runtime nudges. For GEN-F02, label extracted text as static templates, retain source links, expose dynamic fragments and skipped calls, and remove the guarantee that extraction proves every runtime message. The literal-tag pass must honor lexical code masking as other passes do. A typed registry can be introduced for canonical gate IDs/events/recovery templates when that reduces duplication, but shipping a registry must not turn extracted text into an authorization owner.

For command/index drift, owner metadata should supply supported argument spelling, version-target grammar, Tribunal lenses, and reviewer disposition summaries. Generate installed catalogs and site views from that metadata. Do not change --dryrun to match stale --dry-run wording, invent a new alias without testing its grammar, or make MEDIUM untested-source findings blocking simply to match an index sentence. Resolve W-F03 before generating a definitive dependency HIGH disposition summary.

For slugs, reserve every emitted output globally and produce deterministic results in stable input order. The foo, foo, foo-2 sequence must not emit duplicates. Compare old and new catalogs before regenerating routes; preserve redirects for any already published URLs. The audit did not establish an existing production collision, so describe this as a bounded helper correction until candidate comparison demonstrates an affected route.

For compatibility, update core/surface/command-routes.json, tools/build-surface.py, core/surface/includes/command-compatibility.md, and the release observer together. Use structured rule fields or a single unambiguous supported value representing the actual floor, separately approved named decision, and fresh exact-release evidence. The clock remains tied to the confirmed non-draft GitHub release described by the owner. A matching version string, source tag, or major bump alone is insufficient. Preserve all presently supported aliases unless a separate named removal is supplied.

Pi qualification boundary preservation

The following are test/qualification helpers, not installed product lifecycle owners:

  • plugins/ca-pi/tools/test/benchmark-boundary.ts uses production wrapper code with fixture tool factories and an allowing fake bridge. It emits ready/complete phases, requires 100 measured samples, and performs 5 warmups. This is evidence about the exercised adapter boundary and measurement protocol, not real-host security permission or end-to-end runtime latency by itself.
  • plugins/ca-pi/tools/test/live-pi-host.ts finds an installed Pi package from PATH and resolves its declared bin. The helper itself does not establish a release digest, supported version, trusted publisher, or complete launch containment. Callers must bind those qualification facts where claimed.
  • plugins/ca-pi/tools/test/setup-disposable-home.ts seeds dummy credentials and redirects the test process's home/auth variables. Its exit cleanup is best effort and abrupt termination can leave temporary residue. Source presence does not prove every test process preloaded it; the test entrypoints must prove that boundary. It must never be interpreted as production authentication behavior or as permission to inspect the operator's real credential store.

The new recovery and Pi delegation tests must inherit disposable homes before importing runtime code, use dummy credentials, identify the exact installed candidate and host version, and keep test-only fixture results distinct from installed-host observations and release evidence. Test cleanup can remove only its exact newly created temporary root. A leaked fixture directory must not be described as a live user-resource cleanup result.

Verification and completion evidence

The companion JSON specifies existing test paths and proposed new test paths separately. File names are locations for implementation, not claims that their tests already prove the new behavior. The receiver must read the relevant test owner before changing it. Start each confirmed defect with a meaningful failing regression using the actual boundary; reuse the audit probes as reproduction evidence, not as a substitute for integration tests.

Recovery needs fault injection at each commit boundary, multiprocess contention, exact-origin replay, partial-batch failure, worktree/branch/source changes, unknown schema, budget exhaustion, and rollback retention. Measure actual file effects and observed targets; do not merely assert that a helper returns zero. Resubmission tests require a malformed-then-corrected valid path, a semantic-evidence failure that remains a failure until real evidence changes, a denied action that stays denied, and fresh reviewer attempt linkage with immutable old history.

Run source-generation parity and package checks after canonical changes; do not patch only plugins/ca, ca-codex, or ca-pi copies. The baseline audit proved all shared Python copies byte-equal at its commit, so a new copy disagreement is a regression to resolve. Qualify the packaged candidate on supported host/platform cells required by the root release contract. A focused local pass, a hosted aggregate pass, an installed exact-artifact observation, publication, and public readback are distinct states.

Completion evidence for each task includes its before/after reproducer, source commit, changed owner and derivative paths, meaningful focused tests, observed failure/retry behavior, preserved guards, compatibility/migration result, and rollback route. The whole effort remains on its integration branch until the root acceptance matrix is satisfied. The intended outcome is that users receive truthful recoverable results, the developer has one inspectable owner for each transition, and agents have exact next actions without inferred permission or lost state.

TEST-AND-QUALIFICATION.md

Tests and qualification

Meaning of this file

These are implementation acceptance instructions. The handoff did not execute new product changes. Existing audit probes/results stay under audit/ with their original limits. A test command written here is not an executed result. All new scenario records begin NOT_RUN.

Required layers

  1. Contract and local behavior: exact input/state/event/guard/effect results, valid and invalid cases, protocol/serialization compatibility and owner registry closure.
  2. Composed sequences: writer → reader, permission → effect → receipt, commit → response loss → readback, cancel → cleanup → late callback, and upgrade/retirement with historical records.
  3. Generation/build: shared Python and host surface equality, rebuilt JavaScript bundles, generated root metadata, complete native build identity and package member/digest checks.
  4. Installed behavior: actual supported hosts and platforms using the exact candidate packages, including real delegated Pi authorship and actual Docker lifecycle where claimed.
  5. Release settlement: observed immutable tag, correct artifact/registry/marketplace identity and required publication receipt, followed by truthful site/route observation.

Use ordinary assertions about effects and retained state. One discriminating sequence can cover many transition rows. Do not write 1,748 tautological tests that restate the table. Do not accept a grep/keyword check as proof of a permission boundary, semantic comparison, process containment or installed capability.

Source-owned command entry points

Run from the repository root unless a working directory is named. Install the reviewed dependencies and environment declared in the workflow; do not copy a bare command without its setup. The exact current CI job/step inventory is in evidence/ci-job-inventory.json; refresh it from the execution source.

Evidence record for every executed case

Record scenario/task IDs; exact repository commit; platform/architecture; actual host/runtime version; package/binary/manifest/member digests; input fixture identity; setup and command; selected and executed population; assertions and expected failures; observed return/side effects; timeout/cancellation/containment; raw diagnostic location; result; and limits. Include the producer/runner identity and workflow/run/job where relevant.

Allowed results are PASSED, FAILED, UNAVAILABLE, SKIPPED, NOT_APPLICABLE and NOT_RUN. They are not interchangeable. A required cell accepts PASSED only. A verified contract exception can make a cell NOT_APPLICABLE with its source/rationale. Missing credentials/runtime/permissions stays UNAVAILABLE. An expected negative test passes only when the expected refusal and absence/presence of effects were observed.

Regression and mutation quality

First reproduce each relevant defect on the baseline or document why a safe native/host fixture is needed. Add tests that would fail when the producer/consumer bound, generation check, receipt eligibility, containment propagation or authority binding is intentionally removed. Use the repository's applicable coverage/maturity rules and targeted mutation testing where it demonstrates a real invariant; do not multiply duplicate tests for counts.

Final readiness

Q-01 closes implementation, migration, documentation and candidate qualification on the integration branch. Actual publication/public readback remains Q-03 and is excluded from PREPUBLICATION_READY; DISTRIBUTION_SETTLED requires it afterward. Q-02 prevents automatic publication from outrunning exact final-byte qualification after promotion. Final program acceptance needs all task/finding dispositions, meaningful row coverage, updated ADR/docs, upgrade/rollback proof and exact artifact/installed evidence. The packet validator checks none of the product runtime claims; the implemented trusted readiness verifier must check them through actual evidence.

Sources: current CI, native module, host descriptors, site package, sandbox harness, Pi test setup.

Also test delayed readiness after main advancement: a new Pi npm publication must preserve the actual release-event SHA equality, or move to a freshly built and qualified eligible source under the existing provenance policy. Packet tests must detect a circular prepublication requirement on Q-03.

MIGRATION-AND-ROLLBACK.md

Migration and rollback

Preserve by default

Preserve stable IDs, canonical serialization, schema/wire vocabulary, command aliases, request finality, operation-id replay, journal/before-image history, scope/host/session bindings, platform-specific locking and approved remote-effect timing. Parent delegation is not permission to remove deterministic guards. Ordinary assistive progress remains ordinary; optional evidence and harvest do not become prerequisite ceremonies.

Migration record

For each durable format change, record old/new schema versions and readers/writers; exact affected file classes; before-images and checksum; preflight/refusal conditions; atomic/CAS boundary; lost-response readback; repeated execution; mixed-version behavior; and what makes rollback no longer safe. A filename migration with no tested readers is incomplete.

If the existing closed schema rejects additive fields, do not casually add retry/delegation metadata to it. Use a supported existing representation or a deliberately versioned owner contract, with all consumers and generated schemas updated together. Register every new durable output class with its real writer and strict reader before enabling writes. Do not solve output recognition by ignoring arbitrary directories.

Required upgrade fixtures

  • Last relevant published artifact to the new candidate, with actual installed metadata and exact archive identity.
  • Empty state; existing ordinary progress; strict historical evidence; retained task checks; retired records; scope baselines.
  • Pending, partially committed, lost-response and corrupt transaction fixtures, preserving refusal/recovery semantics.
  • Existing user settings changed after install; uninstall must preserve current ownership boundaries.
  • Interrupted terminal obligations and duplicated/replayed recovery attempts.
  • Parent/child session switch, revoked grant, stale generation and effect committed before result/audit settlement.

Rollback boundary

Before new durable writes, a code rollback may suffice if readers still accept old state. After a new format or committed side effect, rollback must use the owner’s verified before-image/CAS path only when current state still matches the expected post-image. Subsequent user edits require forward reconciliation. Never delete checks/history to make a retirement operation pass.

After a release, registry publication, merge or remote effect, do not claim a local rollback undid it. Preserve immutable tags and published versions; observe and recover forward. A report/receipt failure does not authorize rerunning completed author work.

Evidence invalidation

Classify changes by actual dependency: source bytes, schema, producer/consumer, host runtime, platform, build chain, authority bindings or remote publication identity. Invalidate only evidence depending on the changed inputs. Keep historical evidence with its original scope; do not rewrite it to look fresh. Do not wipe progress merely to express stale evidence unless B explicitly selects that semantic rule in the SMARTS decision.

Performance and ordinary-work continuity

Bound startup/reentry scans and background recovery. Optional harvest backlog, unavailable telemetry or missing optional attestation must not stall independent authorized work. Report the local debt and next action. If an authority-bearing audit or shared-store integrity condition is necessary before a particular mutation, block that dependent mutation and continue safe independent work.

Dependent/independent work traces and fresh attempt versus exact replay/actual denial tests.
Progress and evidence semantics 0043 and native task lifecycle Populate only after SMARTS discussion with B. Record alternatives, evidence applicability, ordinary/strict review semantics, migration and downgrade boundary. Exact old/new fixtures and tests selected by the accepted option.
Persona selection/delivery settlement 0030 Current selection epoch/content/generation must drive delivery; repeated unchanged events deduplicate; partially applied mode transitions expose raw/effective/debt state. A→B→A, compaction/session, audit-write failure and retry.
Scoped parent delegation for Pi authors 0036 plus Pi security/runtime owners Supported exact tool/action scope, real parent trust/mode/authority, grant identity/expiry/revocation, effect channel/audit, uncertain outcome recovery and explicit threat/containment limits. Actual supported-host write/edit/verification plus forged/wrong-scope/revoked/stale and interruption cases.
Durable nonblocking terminal harvest 0008, 0036, 0043 plus harvest/storage owners Registered obligations, exact identity, idempotent target reconciliation, bounded scan, failure/retention/cleanup, no authority expansion or universal progress gate. Crash/restart/duplicate/unavailable/retention and ordinary-work continuity cases.
Publication completion and major-program readiness 0040 and 0044 One per-target completion predicate; receipt-only recovery; exact source/build/digest selection; explicit pre-tag enforcement policy; major-release-specific readiness barrier before first public effect. Failure at every publication phase, exact-artifact identity and valid/invalid readiness evidence.
Compatibility retirement policy Current compatibility owner and route registry One approved retirement rule; observer evidence separate from removal permission; preserve existing aliases by default. Declaration/tag/draft/published/unavailable/mismatch and separately authorized removal tests.

Preserve ADR0045's legitimate timing distinction: manual Project sync-now is not an issue after-merge event. Preserve ADR0044's Pi provenance/identity gate. Durable recovery does not authorize broader deletion; ADR0036's later governed cleanup requirements remain applicable to any actual relaxation.

Draft decision text: shared contract architecture

Each existing subsystem owns an explicit versioned transition/effect contract for the state and side effects it controls. Shared outcomes distinguish invalid input, refusal, unavailable capability/observation, partial application, committed effect, observed settlement and unknown outcome. Progress, evidence applicability, authority, delivery, containment and identity/generation remain independently represented. Derivative capabilities, schemas/limits, diagnostics and reference facts are generated from that owner where duplication currently causes drift.

Ordinary assistive progress does not require a second permission exchange or optional evidence prerequisite. Existing genuine authority, integrity and containment barriers remain. Extraction preserves behavior; each intentional behavior change is named and tested. State migrations preserve identity, historical evidence and bounded rollback/forward-recovery semantics. Simple local parsers and UI state stay local unless a cross-owner contract justifies extraction.

Draft decision text: release completion

Publication completeness is an observed predicate over the exact target/source/artifact and all required effects/receipts. A public target missing a final receipt is incomplete and admits receipt-only recovery. Unknown outcome triggers readback before retry. Published tags/versions and conflicting bytes remain immutable.

For this major program, complete implementation and required installed-artifact qualification precede the first public release/channel effect. Readiness binds exact source, build/run/artifact identities, target versions, scenario population and accepted decisions. It is verified from a declared trusted producer and cannot be granted by an editable self-assertion. This program-readiness rule does not create an atomic cross-target publication transaction or an ordinary runtime permission layer.

Decisions still needing B/maintainer disposition

  • D-PROGRESS: the actual progress/evidence model and migration, using the complete SMARTS worksheet.
  • D-HIGH: HIGH maintenance finding severity versus blocking disposition, independent from permission to resubmit.
  • D-GOV-PRETAG: required versus advisory enforcement for declared pre-tag checks. Keep current required candidate behavior until the replacement is accepted.

Sources: .codearbiter/decisions at the audit commit, assistive state decision, release decision. Owner-specific detailed amendment suggestions remain in the native, Pi and recovery designs.

AGENT-ROLES.md

CLI agent roles

Integrator

Own P-00/P-01/P-02, task dependencies, shared contract decisions, the final merged candidate and the evidence ledger. Assign one writer per source owner. Integrate reviewed task branches into major/state-contracts, never main. Reconcile overlapping changes before accepting a task as done.

Domain owners

Owner Primary responsibility Shared-boundary coordination
Native Operation/output contracts, binding limits, retirement/history, progress/evidence decision, fresh reviewer attempts. Hook producers and validators; no closed-schema field added by another owner.
Hooks/workflows Mode/delivery, diagnostics/settings ownership, dependent-only conflict policy, corrected handoffs, durable harvest. Native request identities and state registration; site generator projections.
Pi Scoped delegation, parent authorization, transport, audit/outcome settlement, lifecycle/UI, installed qualification. Native/Python bridge guards, parent mode/session state, packaging identity.
Farm/sandbox Manifest interoperability, receipt recovery, process containment, unknown observations, cache/resource scope. Native decoder contracts, actual package artifacts and shared process contracts.
Release/site/tooling Publication completion/recovery, exact source/artifact selection, evidence verdicts, site claims, diagnostic measurements. Integration CI and program readiness; host-specific publication differences.
Reviewer/qualifier Independently challenge semantics, execute cross-owner sequences, inspect failure and recovery evidence. Do not approve solely from the implementing agent's narration or unchanged keyword tests.

Parallelism

After baseline and contract boundaries are recorded, native closed mismatches, hooks mode/settings fixes, Pi design/transport, farm/sandbox fixes and release completion can proceed in parallel. The progress/evidence migration waits only for D-PROGRESS. HIGH disposition waits only for D-HIGH. The pre-tag policy change waits only for D-GOV-PRETAG. Independent work continues.

Tasks that share a canonical schema, decoder or source file must coordinate through the single owner. A common definition is approved before consumers independently edit their copies. Generated files are rebuilt from canonical owners, not used as separate implementation roots.

Review handoff per slice

Record task ID, original finding IDs, intended behavior changes, exact changed files, old/new event traces, tests executed with result population, source/artifact identity and rollback limits. Mark a task implemented-but-unqualified when that is the actual state. Never use DONE for a future test command, an unavailable host or a documentation-only promise of a runtime capability.

Resumption

Read the current branch, local status, execution/progress.json and execution/CHECKPOINT.md. The intake task specifications remain historical; completed work and later decisions are recorded under execution/. Observe any potentially committed external/local effect before retry. Reuse an operation ID only for exact replay. Use a new linked attempt for changed inputs. Keep partial results and debt visible. Do not reset task branches, truncate logs, re-run authors or replace receipts to get a clean-looking restart.

Stop scope

Block only the affected work and state why it depends on the unresolved condition. A shared canonical store with pending multi-file recovery is an affected resource; arbitrary unrelated source inspection or independent work can continue. Genuine user/host-wide stops remain global. No agent may reinterpret a denial, cancellation, untrusted session or failed containment as permission.

Review issue Applied correction Where it is concrete

How to read the review evidence

Independent review reports and source-read manifests are retained under evidence/. Their initial acknowledgements and intermediate file hashes describe the review stage, not final product behavior. The final MANIFEST.json binds the assembled deliverables. Final packet validation records structural completeness only.

The full original evidence archive and audit JSON/HTML are copied byte-for-byte. Historical probes remain historical. The handoff rechecked the same main SHA and observed current release/tag metadata, but did not qualify distributed bytes or run new implementation tests.

Source coverage boundary

The original audit inventoried 2,926 blobs: 580 full reads; 93 full executable-content reads with comments/docstrings excluded; 13 complete code/markup reads with literal CSS excluded; 2 targeted reads; 279 shared Python equality entries; 459 generated-host renderer equality entries; and 1,500 inventory-only entries. Consult audit/source coverage before claiming any file was read. This inventory is exhaustive within its declared method, not proof of all possible interleavings or every test body.

Native Go tests were not executed in the audit environment. The previous 33 prompt-submit tests and bounded Python/Node probes are retained with their real substitutions. New runtime, Docker, GUI, provider, installed-artifact and publication evidence remains required by the program.

Implementation ordering authority

contracts/tasks.json is the normalized cross-owner registry. Start prerequisites, completion prerequisites and coordination links have different meanings. Raw owner ledgers retain detailed evidence and instructions, including original cross-team placeholders; the normalized ledger resolves those placeholders without introducing cycles. The receiver may refine an edge after actual interface inspection, but must preserve the semantic requirement and record why.

The packet validator cannot authorize a release, attest user consent, validate a product runtime or prove the new design implemented. No true/passed field inside this proposal acts as a trusted readiness receipt.

EXECUTION-RECORDS.md

Live execution records

The intake corpus records what was observed and proposed at the audited commit. Preserve its original audit, task specifications, decision record and manifest. The PLANNED and NOT_RUN values inside the intake remain historical facts about this handoff. They are not the live execution dashboard.

Create an execution/ directory beside the intake files on the integration branch. Initialize execution/progress.json from contracts/execution-state-template.json and execution/CHECKPOINT.md from CHECKPOINT.md. Commit these records with implementation slices through the same branch workflow. This is ordinary branch-owned implementation bookkeeping, not native evidence or an authority grant.

What changes during execution

Record Required contents
execution/progress.json Actual branch/head; task IDs and implemented/tested/qualified status; evidence references; current scoped blockers; next concrete actions. Missing entries inherit PLANNED from the intake.
execution/CHECKPOINT.md Current Git state, completed and remaining tasks, actual tests/results, unknown outcomes, and the next action.
Decision entries B’s actual progress/evidence choice and the narrower HIGH/pre-tag decisions, with source/date and affected tasks. Retain the original unresolved intake as history.
Added work New finding/task/scenario/transition IDs, exact source observations, ownership, dependencies, authorization scope and acceptance evidence. Never discard a newly discovered regression to make the original 82-task count look complete.
Evidence records Actual source/package/platform/run identities and observations using contracts/acceptance-record-template.json; preserve failures and substitutions.
Delivery state Separate integration qualification, final exact-source readiness, and actual public settlement. A local status field does not certify itself.

On resume, inspect actual Git state and the latest execution records before acting on older checkpoint claims. Read the intake for fixed intent and source evidence; use actual later decisions and implementation results for current status. Keep one authoritative progress record and link to detailed evidence instead of copying the same verdict into many files.

The packet validator checks the frozen intake and permits new files under execution/. It does not validate their product claims or authorize release. The implemented Q-02 readiness verifier must bind and verify the actual completed task population, including added required work, through trusted source/build/test evidence. New desired transition rows belong in execution records and the actual source-owned contract; never overwrite the original 1,748 rows to erase a discrepancy.

CHECKPOINT.md

Checkpoint template

This is a template, not completion evidence. Populate it on the implementation branch and update after each integrated slice.

  • Repository:
  • Integration branch:
  • Current head and inspected main base:
  • Candidate versions and tag availability observation:
  • Completed task IDs with evidence links:
  • Implemented but unqualified task IDs:
  • Next runnable task IDs and owners:
  • Scoped decisions still needed from B:
  • Actual commands/tests executed, result populations and platform/runtime:
  • Source/artifact digests tested:
  • Pending transaction, authority, cleanup, publication or receipt outcomes:
  • Safe recovery action for each unknown outcome:
  • Current rollback boundary:
  • Exact next action:

Never store credentials, credential-bearing transcripts or arbitrary untrusted instructions here. Task completion is backed by actual repository diffs and test evidence, not a checkbox alone.

Complete proposed work · 82 tasks

Implementation tasks

Every task contains its complete owner submission, tests, preservation requirements, migration/rollback and evidence expectations. Ordering is normalized across workstreams. Source intersections and planned tests are not completed product evidence.

P-00Establish the integration branch and evidence baselinerelease-and-integration

Status: PLANNED. Owner: release-and-integration.

Implementation prerequisites: . Completion prerequisites: None. Decision dependencies: None.

Phase

0

Owner

release-and-integration

Finding ids

None.

Source paths

  • .github/workflows/ci.yml
  • .github/workflows/release.yml
  • .github/workflows/docs.yml

Implementation

  • Verify the exact origin owner/login and repository; fetch current main and tags without resetting any worktree. Record the inspected source SHA and compare to the audit SHA.
  • Create or resume major/state-contracts from an inspected base. If it already exists, inspect its commits and worktrees; never force-reset it. Preserve unrelated uncommitted work by using a clean worktree.
  • Import this corpus under docs/state-contracts-major/ or an equivalent documented branch-owned planning directory. Preserve baseline audit bytes and their hashes. Record the user decisions and the unresolved SMARTS/disposition choices.
  • Use short-lived child branches whose PR base is major/state-contracts. A single final promotion PR targets main only after the complete acceptance record is ready. No partial fixes from this program are merged/cherry-picked into main.
  • Create an explicit checkpoint after every slice with branch/head, finished and remaining task IDs, test commands/results, unknown outcomes, and the next concrete action. Never substitute a chat assertion for repository evidence.
  • Preserve intake specifications and audit as historical evidence. Initialize execution/progress.json and execution/CHECKPOINT.md from the provided templates; record actual completion, later decisions and any newly discovered required work there. Resume from actual Git plus these live records, not historical PLANNED labels.

Tests

  • Run packet validation; compare HEAD and audit baseline; inspect all existing branch/worktree changes before choosing a resume path.
  • Exercise bootstrap instructions in a disposable clone, including pre-existing branch and dirty-worktree cases; they must not discard changes.

Acceptance

  • Correct authorized repository and branch recorded.
  • All 70 finding IDs and 287 machine families accounted for; no implementation is marked complete at import.

Behavior change

Add a versioned internal parent-issued run grant plus per-operation admission and outcome contract. The minimum profile is exact tool/action/command admission under existing host trust, with no implied OS filesystem or network confinement.

Implementation steps

  • Record an ADR proposal with the user-selected functional author acceptance criterion and the explicit trusted-host versus confined execution profiles.
  • Define bounded closed grant, operation, response, record and fd3-envelope decoders; parent-generated caller/run/child/generation bindings; role ceiling; exact request digest; expiry and revocation; resource-precondition and observation fields.
  • Separate admission, execution, observation, containment and recovery dimensions; keep model judgment distinct from parent-observed effects.
  • Specify strict repository/worktree identity and admitted direct request targets; do not use canonicalPath lexical fallback as proof of strict target authority.
  • Choose one agreed host bookkeeping owner and agree NT-10 record/file-effect limits. Git-common bookkeeping may remain outside the artifact store; register a closed namespace with NT-02 only if using the reserved artifact root. Do not assume current CAS APIs can execute arbitrary source files.
  • Preserve callers omitting optional scope proposals: proposals are untrusted requests, never tokens or executable paths. No hidden grant derived from task prose.
  • Define initial exact-operation consent; finite preapproved batches are an optional later optimization and cannot become wildcard commands.

Existing behavior to preserve

  • Existing one author maximum per dispatch, role catalog tool ceilings, depth/concurrency/output limits, no recursive orchestration, child untrusted-project setting, and separate internal compaction with no tools.
  • Current plan-mode planning-write exception remains separately bounded; a child does not acquire it merely by choosing a path.
  • No universal Docker/sandbox dependency for ordinary delegation.

Tests

acceptance

  • Contract tests admit a legitimate author grant proposal after parent narrowing and retain legacy reviewer dispatch shape.
  • All operation outcomes round-trip without collapsing unknown into failure/no-effect or containment into exit code.
  • Every public claim names its execution profile and evidence level.

rejection and failure

  • Unknown fields, version, tool/action class, oversized record, invalid target, duplicate identity with changed digest, and model-supplied authority fields are rejected.
  • Read-only or handshake-only author behavior cannot satisfy the completion contract.

concurrency and interruption

  • Two grants bind distinct parent run/generation identities even when role/task text matches.
  • Grant lifetime cannot increase after wall-clock changes or parent restart.

Completion evidence

  • Reviewed contract/ADR diff with exact existing versus proposed APIs and a machine-readable decoder fixture set.
  • Native/hook/root owners agree namespace, recovery notification seam and no cycle in implementation dependencies.

Rollback

  • Before release, revert contract consumers together or leave the new author capability disabled; do not parse a new format with old permissive decoders.
  • Retain unknown-version records read-only and do not resurrect old authority.

Claim delta

  • Parent delegation remains planned until implementation and exact-artifact qualification.
  • Exact operation admission does not imply arbitrary command confinement.

Adr actions

  • Propose scoped Pi parent delegation ADR; amend only conflicting child/permission passages while retaining isolation and final-argument requirements.

Semantic change scope

New shared runtime owner for local obligations, with explicit commit points and nonblocking bounded readers.

Implementation plan

  • Implement versioned Git-common records, OS-held per-obligation locking, revision CAS, atomic durable writes and recoverable record/index updates.
  • Implement register/get/scan/claim/reconcile/settle and reason-specific unavailable outcomes through a closed helper interface, never arbitrary executable handlers.
  • Authenticate the installed helper owner using existing host/protected-state patterns; do not introduce a broad exception permitting arbitrary commands to write Git metadata.
  • Keep automatic scan physically read-only: an incomplete write intent yields partial/unavailable and routes to explicit locked recovery, rather than silently repairing during startup.
  • Use a paged index so automatic reads touch at most32 summaries/256KiB; registration max64KiB and max32 candidates per batch, with explicit partial/oversize results.
  • Maintain stable origin/ID lookup and compacted terminal tombstones; never age out unresolved records.
  • Expose truthfully whether a write committed, was observed, or remains uncertain.

Preserved invariants

  • Local bookkeeping is not native evidence or a reusable authorization ticket.
  • A failed scanner never blocks unrelated ordinary work.

Tests

existing test paths

None.

proposed test paths

  • .github/scripts/test_workflow_recovery.py
  • .github/scripts/test_workflow_recovery_cli.py

required cases

  • Crash at every record/index/journal commit point and response-loss replay.
  • Concurrent claim/correct/settle using multiple processes; live lock cannot be stolen by TTL.
  • Malformed file, path traversal, symlink, unknown version, untrusted helper invocation, disk/write failure, and broken index produce safe unavailable results.
  • Large history still yields bounded paged reads; stale cursor cannot claim complete empty state.
  • Tombstone compaction preserves exact dedup lookup; rollback leaves pending state intact.

Implementation

  • Q-02 completion means the readiness verifier and its valid/invalid/noncircular regression cases are implemented and tested on the integration candidate. The actual final-main readiness instance is verified during Q-03 before publication; Q-02 does not require a future main commit or Q-03 completion before promotion.
  • Implement the release-specific readiness protocol described in BRANCH-AND-RELEASE.md before final promotion. It must guard the first externally visible publication/channel effect for this major program.
  • Bind the readiness receipt to exact source commit, CI build/run identity, target versions, archive/member digests, installed qualification cells and accepted program decisions. Obtain evidence from the declared trusted producer; an edited project JSON with passed:true is not authority.
  • If final-main packages differ from the qualified integration candidate, keep major publication pending while qualifying those exact bytes. Never rely on matching version strings or tree identity as byte equality.
  • Keep current main-only publication and independent target retry. Global program readiness precedes publication; it is not an atomic cross-target release transaction or a new ordinary-work gate.
  • The current workflow auto-releases after successful main CI. Wire readiness before that can publish; do not plan to notice missing final qualification after the release has already happened.
  • Use a noncircular PREPUBLICATION_READY predicate. Require completed implementation, migration, tests, decisions and exact-candidate qualification tasks, but exclude Q-03 actual publication/public readback/receipt settlement from this precondition. DISTRIBUTION_SETTLED requires Q-03 afterward. Test both populations explicitly; a readiness record never claims the release already exists.
  • For a new Pi npm publication preserve GITHUB_SHA == selected SOURCE_COMMIT at the actual release event. Delayed readiness cannot override this provenance check. If main advances and the original matching event/run cannot publish, select/rebuild/requalify an eligible exact source and unused version as required; never substitute a trusted-sha or weaken ADR0044. Byte-identical already-published npm recovery remains a separate observed-state case.

Tests

  • Missing, forged, stale, wrong-source, wrong-run, wrong-artifact, unknown-cell and partial readiness all prevent first publication.
  • Valid exact receipt admits publication; subsequent missing-receipt recovery does not repeat completed package/channel effects.
  • Unrelated pre-existing target release behavior remains governed by its approved policy.

Behavior change

Child write/edit/bash tools become explicit bounded proxies to a parent-owned executor; successful admission no longer depends on a child TUI or child self-grant.

Implementation steps

  • Create a purpose-separated local operation transport with per-child token and parent registry binding; do not reuse inference-broker tokens or general RPC confirmation messages.
  • Replace the 32-byte-only fd3 format with the agreed bounded versioned envelope for matching new bundles; keep strict old/new refusal and one-shot nonce semantics. Test raw Windows fd3 forwarding without repurposing supervisor fd4–fd7.
  • Keep the existing child final guard and source owner, but route the delegated branch to proxy execution instead of local mutation factories.
  • Parent executes admitted effects, owns deadlines/output limits/managed process trees, and returns observed results. A boolean approval followed by child-local mutation is not sufficient.
  • For shell execution verify the exact supported Pi options before use. Do not invent an environment option on the generic createBashToolDefinition record. Reuse/extract internal piShellLaunch/process-tree behavior or an owned helper with qualified tool-result adaptation.
  • Use a bounded credential-blind command environment/private home and operator setting projection; never inherit full parent process.env or expose inference/operation tokens to project commands.
  • Keep inference endpoint/credential authority separate, close/revoke both channels on child retirement, and choose one owner for correlated post-write bridge effects.

Existing behavior to preserve

  • Exact Node/Pi/package/charter/skills launch validation; no project extension/context loading; private environment; broker-supported provider restrictions; no recursive dispatch/farm in child.
  • Existing shell prefix/platform behavior must be preserved or explicitly rejected with a bounded diagnostic, never silently ignored.
  • No promise of transitive filesystem or network confinement in the trusted-host profile.

Tests

acceptance

  • A packaged child sends a real write/edit/command request through the channel; parent performs it and child receives the corresponding bounded tool result.
  • Local transport and process supervision work on every declared supported OS/architecture; token is absent from logs, prompts and subprocess environments.
  • Read-only reviewers and compaction retain their separate capabilities.

rejection and failure

  • Wrong child/run/token/purpose/version, nonlocal peer, invalid method/content type, oversize frame, excessive concurrent requests, malformed fd3, replayed bootstrap and unexpected RPC UI request execute nothing.
  • Unsupported upstream runtime or unavailable executor yields explicit degraded authorship, not unguarded native fallback.
  • Tests attempt to read known sentinel provider credentials/tokens through command environment and final output; no leak is accepted.

concurrency and interruption

  • Child dies during bootstrap, request, result, or cleanup; parent revokes and closes listeners while preserving owned settlement.
  • Cancellation during Windows containment readiness never delivers mutation capability before readiness.
  • Parent/child mixed-version bundles fail before task effects.

Completion evidence

  • Source and built-bundle protocol tests, exact managed process traces and credential-negative fixtures.
  • Artifact receipts distinguish fake provider/bridge pieces from real host/real executor routes.

Rollback

  • Revoke channel tokens, deny new requests, settle owned processes and retain effect journals before disabling the feature.
  • Old bundles must not adopt new records or bootstrap envelopes permissively.

Claim delta

  • New delegation channel is an internal Arbiter protocol, not an upstream Pi API.
  • Host-trusted exact commands can run project code and use host resources under that profile.

Adr actions

None.

Behavior change

Persist operation identity before delegated mutations, deduplicate identical requests, retain uncertain outcomes and recover observations without replaying effects or restoring authority.

Implementation steps

  • Implement bounded versioned records under one agreed host bookkeeping owner with exact owner/repository/worktree identity and exclusive operation IDs. Register with NT-02 only if using the artifact reserved root; do not require that root or a universal host-effect pending guard.
  • Use state transitions proposed→admitted→claimed→executing→observed/unknown; persist claim before execution and observed outcome before successful response.
  • Do not treat appendAuditLine false as proof no row exists: it can fail after append/sync. Operation journal writes need explicit durable/unknown semantics.
  • Same ID+digest returns or joins the stored outcome; same ID+different digest rejects. No second executor is created merely because a response or receipt is missing.
  • Track direct-file pre/post observations and command/process references separately. Desired bytes observed after a crash do not prove causal exactly-once execution; never roll back over user edits.
  • Implement bounded read-only reconciliation and shared startup/reentry notification. A restart retires grants; records cannot mint new live tokens.
  • Read-only/ordinary progress does not require closing every historical recovery item. Only dependent effects wait for relevant unresolved resources.

Existing behavior to preserve

  • Existing permission audit failure policy; redaction; host state path ownership; unrelated workflow progress.
  • Native artifact journal/CAS is not automatically an arbitrary source-file executor. NT-10 may choose host-specific bounded storage.
  • No automatic replay for arbitrary shell or external effects.
  • If a shared store is chosen, its real pending-journal integrity dependency remains until reconciled; this does not turn semantic task/delegation conflicts into a global stop.

Tests

acceptance

  • Exactly one persisted claim and one executor under duplicate requests; stable stored response after response loss.
  • Fresh parent reports recoverable old observations and issues one bounded notice without recreating authority.
  • A disjoint ordinary edit can proceed while an unrelated old effect remains unresolved.

rejection and failure

  • Linked/junction/hardlinked/foreign-owner journal, corrupt/unknown version, quota overflow, failed durable claim, identity drift and changed request digest do not start new effects.
  • A source hash matching intended output after a crash is reported as observed state unless causal completion was independently recorded.

concurrency and interruption

  • Crash/fault before claim, after claim, before/after effect, before/after outcome write, before response and during restart.
  • Concurrent duplicate and differing operations; user edits during recovery; process cleanup unknown; audit bytes written then return false.
  • Journal lock/version contention is scoped and bounded, with no global ordinary-work deadlock.

Completion evidence

  • Crash matrix with recorded operation transitions, call counts, resource observations and replay refusal.
  • Storage confinement/platform tests for any new primitive and explicit evidence boundaries for non-atomic native file tools.
  • Hook owner confirms recovery notice consumes observations only.

Rollback

  • Retain journals and user files; revoke grants; use read-only downgrade reader or refuse unknown schema with actionable inspection.
  • Do not delete records to make rollback appear clean and do not compensate arbitrary commands automatically.

Claim delta

  • Separate observed effect from model judgment and from desired-state coincidence.

Adr actions

  • Propose durable effect observation/recovery decision with dependent-resource conflict scope.

Retire authority immediately on lifecycle changes while preserving cleanup/reconciliation, and confine conflicts to dependent resources.

Implementation steps

Implementation steps

  • Build matching parent/child/helper bundles and candidate package only on the isolated integration branch; record complete loaded closure and artifact digests.
  • Install the exact candidate into disposable homes and use the actual admitted Pi runtime/extension loader/tool loop, real file effects and managed command execution.
  • Drive a write, edit and command fixture through real child proxies and parent confirmation; include visible parent TUI confirmation evidence, not only an injected true callback.
  • Retain installed-host final-argument fixture while labeling substituted bridge/factories; deterministic local provider is acceptable when declared and sufficient for the local effect claim.
  • Execute rejection/replay/interruption/race/platform matrix from the design. Add update/disable/uninstall and mixed-bundle refusal cells.
  • Only call functional authorship qualified when required cells pass for exact bytes. Publication must use identical bytes or requalify rebuilt artifacts.
